newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Zaire lifts ban on U.N. food planes for refugees.
newsitem.headline: Zaire lifts ban on U.N. food planes for refugees.

text.p: Zaire has lifted its ban on foreign-registered aircraft delivering food supplies to refugees in the eastern part of the country, the World Food Programme said on Wednesday.

The Zairean government suspended the airlifts on Jan. 30 but it had prevented some WFP large transport planes from landing since last November, forcing the agency to rely on scarce Zairean-registered aircraft or small planes.
"This is a significant breakthrough," said WFP spokesman Trevor Rowe in a statement from the Rome-based agency issued here. "Now we hope to more than double our daily deliveries."

WFP estimates the minimum food needs of 200,000 refugees in eastern Zaire to be about 100 tonnes a day. At the moment only about 30 tonnes a day has been reaching 160,000 refugees in Tingi Tingi, Amisi and Lubutu.
Rowe said that WFP was now in the process of chartering an Ilushin-76 to supplememt its Boeing 707 which would resume service on Feb. 6.
But he said that WFP, in transporting larger amounts of food into Kisangani airport, still faced difficulties in delivering the supplies because of poor road conditions.
